Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Medial RIGHT knee pain for the past 2 months
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Mild amount of reactive marrow edema at the medial femoral condyle. Marginal osteophytes are noted at the distal femur, proximal tibia, and patella. No acute fracture. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Diffuse chondral thinning along the anterior weightbearing and focal full thickness chondral loss at the margin of medial femoral condyle. The tibial plateau cartilage is normal.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal. Small intraosseous ganglion at the tibial attachment of the posterior cruciate ligament.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Mild thickening of the medial collateral ligament with trace periligamentous edema consistent with degenerative MCL signal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Osteoarthritis with full thickness chondral loss involving the medial femoral condyle and subchondral reactive edema.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Knee pain, injury 2 years prior.
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.  

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: 
Alignment is anatomic.  No acute fracture. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process.  No aggressive osseous lesions.  

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion with mild synovial proliferation. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst. 

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Extensive complex tear of the body, posterior horn and root. Maceration and extrusion of the body. Mild reactive edema adjacent tibial plateau along the medial joint line. 
Medial compartment cartilage: Progression of diffuse high grade cartilage loss with areas of full-thickness cartilage loss along the weight-bearing femoral condyle and tibial plateau.  

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal. 
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defect.  

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT: 
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Redemonstration of cartilage loss and full-thickness fissuring of the patella. Some increased cartilage loss of the trochlea. 

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.  
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.  

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema which may represent low grade sprain or reactivate edema from medial meniscus tear.  
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.  
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal. 

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild quadriceps insertion tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: Mild patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.  
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad.  No lateral patellar tilt or translation.  No patella alta.  Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 14 mm. 

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy.  Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact. 

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar soft tissue edema. No soft tissue mass. 
Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. 

IMPRESSION: 
1.	[REDACTED]. 
2.	Medial and patellofemoral compartmental chondrosis, progressed from prior. 
3.	Periligamentous edema about the medial collateral ligament which may represent low grade sprain or reactivate edema from medial meniscus tear.
4.	Small left knee effusion with synovial proliferation.

Findings: No significant knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  Normal tibiofemoral articular cartilage. There is mild - moderate thinning of the medial patellar facet articular cartilage but no underlying bony change. The rest of the patellofemoral articulation is unremarkable.  Conclusion: No meniscal tear. Medial patellar facet articular cartilage degeneration as described.

Findings:  Small joint effusion. No sinister bone marrow changes.  Full-thickness tear of the ACL at the femoral attachment. Intact PCL. Intact collateral ligaments.  Complex tearing of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with displaced meniscal fragments extending posteriorly, adjacent to the tibial attachment of the PCL. Intact lateral meniscus.  Intact extensor mechanism. No evidence of fat pad impingement.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, popliteus tendon, distal biceps femoris tendon and distal iliotibial band.  Full-thickness chondral loss along the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle with underlying bone stress change. High-grade chondral thinning is also noted in the medial tibial condyle. Relatively well-maintained lateral tibiofemoral and patellofemoral hyaline articular cartilage.  
Conclusion:  Full-thickness rupture of the ACL at the femoral attachment. Complex tearing of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with displaced meniscal fragments extending posteriorly, adjacent to the tibial attachment of the PCL. Severe medial tibiofemoral degenerative changes.

Findings:  There is a mild knee effusion. Normal appearances of the medial meniscus. Most of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is absent and I suspect is found flipped anteriorly.  ACL is ruptured. There is moderate anterior translation of the lateral tibial plateau in relation to femur. Normal PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  There is a small focus of cartilage thinning - loss in the weightbearing aspect of the lateral tibial condyle. Normal medial tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage.  Conclusion: Old ACL rupture. Anterior translation of the lateral tibial plateau in relation to femur is noted indicating instability. Anterior flipping of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Knee pain, patellar tracking disorder, patellar tendinopathy.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the     knee was performed on a     system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Physiologic joint fluid without large volume joint effusion. No ossified intra-articular bodies. No significant Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal full-thickness cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal full-thickness cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Near full-thickness fissuring along the medial patella facet (series 2, image 15; series 4, image 15).

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No high-grade tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No high-grade tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No suspicious edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No significant lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy.    

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1. Mild patellofemoral chondrosis.

MRI of Left Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, CO T2W FS, SG T1W, AX T2W FS

* The contour of PCL is not all in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside, R/O tear.
   In favor of avulsion fracture of PCL insertion site of posterior intercondylar eminence.
* Interstitial intermediate signal in ACL on T1WI, R/O grade 1 injury.
* Hyperintensity signal is noted in distal quadriceps femoris tendon, especially at patellar insertion site, reflecting patella enthesophytes and tendinosis of distal quadriceps tendon.
* Focal hyperintensity area is noted in tibial tuberosity, intercondylar area, and posterior of medial condyle on F/S T2WI,  reflecting bone contusion.
* Spur formation of knee joint with mild subchondral edema in medial aspect of knee joint and irregular thin articular cartilage, reflecting osteoarthritis.
    Wearing of articular cartilage of patella, reflecting grade 3-4 patellar chondromalacia. 
* Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
* Subcutaneous edema around knee, more prominent at lateral side.
* Muscle and intermuscular infiltration over left popliteal fossa, in favor of muscle and intermusclar edema.
* Deep infrapatellar bursitis.
* Thickening of iliotibial band and quadriceps tendon, in favor of tendinosis.

Impression:
1. C/W tear of PCL and avulsion fracture of PCL with bone marrow edema in proximal tibia. 
2. Osteoarthritis of left knee.
3. Synovitis of left knee with suprapatellar bursitis and deep infrapatellar bursitis; patellar plicae.
3. Subcutaneous edema around left knee and muscle and intermuscular edema over popliteal fossa. Mild popliteus and Anserine bursitis.
4. Grade 1 injury of ACL.
5. Bone contusion over left proximal tibia.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

CONSTATATIONS :

Fractures :
Aucune.

Alignement articulaire :
Normal.

Changements dégénératifs :
Arthrose médiale légère à modérée, arthrose fémoropatellaire modérée et arthrose latérale légère avec chondropatie proportionnelle globale. Des foyers de chondropatie sévère ont été notés au niveau de l'apex patellaire et de la facette médiale, ainsi qu'au niveau du condyle fémoral médial portant, avec un œdème réactionnel de la moelle osseuse associé.

Signal de la moelle osseuse : Par ailleurs normal.

Ligament croisé antérieur : Normal.
Ligament croisé postérieur : Normal.
Ligament collatéral médial : Normal.
Complexe du ligament collatéral latéral : normal.

Ménisque médial : Normal.
Ménisque latéral : Normal.

Tendons extenseurs : Normal.
Rétinacula patellaire : Normal.
Pes anserinus : Normal.

Coin postéro-médial et postéro-latéral : Normal.

Épanchement articulaire : Minuscule épanchement articulaire non significatif.
Kyste de Baker : Aucun.

Autres trouvailles significatives :
Petit kyste ganglionnaire non significatif à la jonction myotendineuse du muscle poplité.

CONCLUSION :
Arthrose tricompartimentale légère à modérée, plus importante dans les compartiments médial et fémoropatellaire, telle que décrite.
Pas de déchirure méniscale ou ligamentaire.

Trouvailles:

Il y a un signal normal de la moelle osseuse. Il n'y a pas de fracture ou de contusion. Il y a un léger amincissement du cartilage impliquant les trois compartiments sans région de perte de cartilage complet.

Il y a des changements dégénératifs intrasubstances impliquant le corps et la corne postérieure du ménisque interne. Il y a une déchirure longitudinale d'orientation horizontale s'étendant de la corne postérieure, jusqu'au niveau du corps du ménisque interne. La déchirure s'étend à la surface articulaire inférieure du ménisque. Il y a un petit kyste paraméniscal millimétrique adjacent à la corne postérieure et au corps. Il n'y a pas de fragment déplacé. Le ménisque externe est sans particularité.

Autrement, le mécanisme des extenseurs, le ligament croisé antérieur, le ligament croisé postérieur, le ligament collatéral interne, le semi-membraneux, le muscle et le tendon du poplité, le biceps femoris distal, le ligament collatéral externe et la bandelette ilio-tibiale sont sans particularité.

Conclusion:

1- Rotule sans particularité sans fracture ou contusion. Légers changements dégénératifs des trois compartiments.

2- Changements dégénératifs intrasubstances du ménisque interne avec une déchirure horizontale telle que détaillée ci-haut.

3- Aucune évidence de blessure ligamentaire.
